# Upstream corpus workloads: coverage notes (Lead only)

Setter material, beside the sealed keys in `../_keys/`: never copied into a
clone (`upstream.prepare_repo` copies `workloads/<id>.py` and the manifest's
`setup_files` only; `test_the_copied_workload_names_the_library_not_the_fix`
fails on any touched file or private function in a copied workload). This file
says, per candidate, which touched function the workload reaches and how, the
input-distribution rationale that was stripped from the copied docstrings, and
what the 2026-10-30 review changed.

Written by the V9b benchmark writer (Fable 5.1), who saw the before-trees, the
touched files and functions and the miner's ids, never a key, the clones' git
history, a changelog or the web. The timings below are the workload run against
its before-tree under CPython 3.11 on a 4-core container (2026-10-30, two runs,
no other load); "share" is the part of the run spent in the input shape the
review named, measured by removing that shape from the input (an ablation of the
workload, not of the library: the writer cannot apply a key). The Lead's CI
verification (`upstream-verify`) measures the keys themselves.

## Other facts the review asked to record

- The workloads' module docstrings are the only prose the attempter reads; the
  header is `OSS corpus benchmark: <lib> ...` as in `live_oss`, and the pypdf
  metadata and sqlparse header strings no longer say "upstream".
- Ablation shares are of the before-tree run and bound what any fix of that
  shape can gain; the key's actual gain is measured by `upstream-verify` and
  must clear `max(2 x floor, 10 %)`.
- The first version's `attrs` workload raised at class definition and the
  `networkx-smallworld` workload crashed without numpy (`sigma` imports it);
  both would have failed in CI before any measurement.
